nights.text: Someone has started leaving things under the door at night. Seven minutes of quiet, please. I want to hear who it is.

note.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.

quest.done: Seven minutes, and a soft scrape at the door. Only a moth with a letter. It would not say who sent it.

keepsake.name: A moth-light letter
keepsake.description: Unsigned. Smells faintly of rain and somebody else's kitchen.

nights.text: The moon is nearly round tonight. I should leave something by the door for whoever writes. A seed, or a reply?

options.label: A seed
options.reply: A seed, then. Nobody has ever been annoyed by a seed. I will put it on the mat.
options.later: The seed is gone from the mat. In its place, a small dry leaf. I take this as manners.

options.label: A reply
options.reply: A reply. Yes. I shall keep it short, in case the moth reads over my shoulder.
options.later: I wrote only 'Hello, who is it?' and slid it out. It has not come back. I keep checking the mat.

nights.text: The clocks went back, I hear. One extra hour tonight. I have put it by the kettle, in case someone needs it.

note.text: An hour is a small room. Leave the door open and see who comes in.

nights.text: The moon is full and very pleased with itself. I counted the things on the mat this morning. Still no name, only a damp leaf.
extras: The lamp has gone amber for the autumn. I did not ask it to. I think it just felt the season.
I mended one cloak button today. The other buttons watched and seem to be thinking about it.
The kettle has a new sound this week, a small cough before the whistle. I have decided it is polite.
Cold nose this morning. Good news: the burrow is still exactly where I left it.

nights.text: The letter-writer left a second note, but the ink ran in the damp. Remember something for me, and I will try to remember what it said.
extras: The first proper frost is somewhere close. I can smell it, like a cold coin.
I swept the leaves off the step. They came back in a better arrangement.
The moth sat on the lampshade all evening, reading. I did not like to ask what.
Soup tonight. I tasted it three times, to be fair to it.

note.text: A small light kept burning is a kind of letter to whoever is still out walking.

quest.done: There. Held fast. The ink has dried, and the note says only: keep the lamp lit. I would have done that anyway.

keepsake.name: A smudged note
keepsake.description: Two words legible, a third lost to damp. It smells of moth wing and cold air.

nights.text: I have kept the lamp lit, as the note said. The moth approves. I still do not know who was asking.
extras: Acorns are dropping on the path tonight, like small, polite knocks.
The wool socks came out of the chest today. They remembered me fondly.
I counted my cloak buttons twice. The answer was the same both times, which is all I ask.
The wind tried the door at dusk, then thought better of it.

nights.text: The mat was bare this morning, not even a leaf. I checked twice, then once more to be fair to the mat.
extras: The moon is past its fullest and has begun to lean. I find it restful to watch something take its time.
A good dark evening for jam on bread. The dark did not ask for jam, but it seemed to approve.
I shook out the blue blanket and a whole summer afternoon fell out of it. Just a small one.
The chimney has started humming when the wind turns north. We are both getting used to it.

note.text: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases; it will never pass into nothingness.

nights.text: The moth is back on the lampshade, and it ought to have a name. I am poor at names. What shall we call it?
extras: The last of the pears went soft on the sill. I gave them a respectful send-off, with a spoon.
It is dark before supper now. I have started eating by lamplight and calling it a feast.
There is mist on the path tonight. It is only borrowing the road, I think.
The stairs were chilly on my feet this morning. The wool socks were ready, which I took as friendship.

options.label: Wick
options.reply: Wick. Short, warm, and it sits near the lamp anyway. I think it likes it. It did not leave.
options.later: I called it Wick across the room today. A wing twitched. Either it knows, or it was a draught.

options.label: Mister Dusk
options.reply: Mister Dusk. Very grand. I shall use the full name, and bow slightly. The moth bowed back, I think.
options.later: Mister Dusk has taken the good corner of the lampshade. I did not offer it. It simply expected it.

nights.text: It is the sort of evening that wants sitting through. Seven minutes of quiet, if you can spare them. The moth and I will keep still beside you.
extras: Someone down the lane has carved a turnip into a grumpy face. I saluted it on my way past.
The hedge smells of woodsmoke tonight. I take it as a sign the neighbours are well.
I hung the wet cloak by the fire and it steamed gently, like a small, thoughtful cloud.
The moon is thinning to a half now. It looks like a pared apple, and I will not say what that does to my appetite.
A single late bee came to the window, looked about, and left. I thought it very sensible of it.

note.text: Dark comes early now. That is only the day going to bed. You are welcome to sit with it a while.

quest.done: Seven minutes, kept whole. Even the lamp seemed to listen. I found this on the mat afterward, and I think it is yours.

keepsake.name: A pocket of quiet
keepsake.description: A walnut shell stuffed with wool and sealed with wax. Hold it to your ear and nothing happens, gently.

nights.text: Something new under the door this morning: a drawing of a small lamp, with no words. Whoever it is draws better than they write.
extras: November has arrived without knocking. I put the kettle on to show it where things are.
The hedgehog next door has gone quiet for the winter. I left a thimble of seeds by his hedge, in case of dreams.
I tried the old mittens on. They fit, which is either good luck or a lot of porridge.
The path is all wet leaves now, and each step says its own small word.

nights.text: I have the lamp drawing, and nowhere to put it. Shall it go on the wall, or into the big book? I would like a second opinion.
extras: The kettle and I woke at the same moment. Neither of us would admit who was first.
A fine drizzle of leaves came down the chimney. I treated them as post.
I found a button behind the bread bin. It matches nothing, which makes it very interesting.
The wool socks have started to feel like old colleagues. We nod at each other in the mornings.
The moon is a thin slice tonight. Someone has been at the cheese, and I am not looking at the moth.

note.text: Heaven is under our feet as well as over our heads.

options.label: On the wall
options.reply: On the wall, then. Beside the window, where the lamp can look at itself. I used a very small tack.
options.later: The drawing has been on the wall all day. The moth sat beneath it for an hour, looking up.

options.label: In the big book
options.reply: In the big book, next to the red leaf. They will have a lot to talk about. I pressed the page flat.
options.later: I opened the big book to check on the drawing. It was still there, and the leaf had not objected.

nights.text: The window has fogged over and I am too comfortable to wipe it. Would you tell me what the sky is doing?
extras: The drawing of the lamp has not moved, but I keep feeling it has been looking at something.
I found a walnut in the coat pocket from last year. We regarded each other with mutual surprise.
The porridge pot and I have settled into a quiet winter routine. It involves a lot of stirring and very little talking.
There is a new draught under the pantry door. I have named it the Visitor and given it no tea.

quest.done: Ah, so that is what it has been up to. Thank you. I wiped a small circle in the glass to see for myself, and it was a good circle.

keepsake.name: A fogged button
keepsake.description: A horn button that still seems faintly breathed on. Hold it up, and the room goes soft.

nights.text: Another drawing under the door this morning: a kettle, with steam. Whoever it is has been looking at my kettle. I am flattered and slightly watched.
extras: The moon rises late and thin now. I waited up for it, and it was worth about half a candle.
I swept the leaves off the step. By the time I turned round, they had returned, as if invited.
The bread went hard on the shelf. I have decided it is now a doorstop, and a good one.
A cold nose of wind came in with the post. I asked it to wipe its feet.

note.text: Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.

nights.text: Whoever draws under my door has left no name. Shall I set something out on the mat for them? A cup of tea, or a biscuit?
extras: The frost came in the night and drew ferns on the glass. Very neat work. I did not breathe on it.
The moon is a fine thread before dawn now. I could almost hang a small coat from it.
I found where the draught goes in the afternoons. It sits on the stairs and thinks.
The woollen hat has been promoted from thinking hat to going-out hat. It takes the extra work calmly.

options.label: A cup of tea
options.reply: Tea, then. In the blue cup, with the chip turned away. I set it on the mat and tried not to hover.
options.later: The cup was still on the mat this morning, empty and rinsed. I did not rinse it. I am choosing not to think about that.

options.label: A biscuit
options.reply: A biscuit. The good kind, with the corner already off. I set it on the mat and tiptoed away from my own door.
options.later: The biscuit is gone, and there is a small neat pile of crumbs where it was. It seems the sort who tidies, mostly.

nights.text: A third drawing today: a round window with a light inside. I think it is mine. I held it up to the real one to check.
extras: The frost left the step as white as a tablecloth. I walked on it carefully, out of manners.
The woodpile is lower than I thought. I have decided to be cheerful about it, in small logs.
I found a pin in the rug. It was not looking for me, but we have become friends.
The last leaf on the old stalk is holding on. I admire its grip and have said so.
The moon came up late and curled like an eyelash. I nodded to it, and I think it nodded back.

note.text: Tuck the cold in with a warm lamp and call it a night.

nights.text: I keep muddling the drawings: lamp, kettle, window. Would you remember something for me? It might straighten my thoughts.
extras: The hedge has gone bare enough to see the lane through. I feel a little more watched, and a little more neighbourly.
A dry leaf has been rolling past the door all morning, like a courier with no letters.
I oiled the door hinge. It now opens in silence, which feels slightly like cheating.
The porridge came out lumpy today. I called the lumps dumplings and we all felt better.

quest.done: Lamp, kettle, window. There, in order, and no muddle left. I felt the whole row settle.

keepsake.name: An acorn-cap bookmark
keepsake.description: A tiny acorn cap with a loop of thread, for keeping your place in a long day.

nights.text: No moon tonight, only a dark where it was. Under the door: a drawing of a small hat. Mine, I think. It is a very good hat.
extras: The moon has gone out altogether. I am told it is only resting, which I respect.
The stars look brighter without the moon about. They seem to have been waiting for the room.
There is woodsmoke on the air from down the lane. Someone is thinking about winter, and so am I.
I trimmed the lamp wick with great ceremony. It burns exactly as before, but I feel better.
Sunday has a quiet shape. I have been walking round it in my slippers.

note.text: A small light kept in is better than a large one left out.

nights.text: The moth has settled on the lamp shade and will not be moved. It wants a name, and mine are all used up. Would you choose one?
extras: Wet leaves on the step make a sound like slow applause. I bowed, in case.
I turned the sock drawer out looking for the other sock. The drawer is now tidier than the sock deserves.
There is a cold edge to the air that smells of tin and chimney. I like it, in small doses.
The kettle took a little longer today. I think it was thinking about something.
I put a second blanket on the chair. The chair did not say anything, but it looked grateful.

options.label: Wick
options.reply: Wick. It suits a creature that sits by a flame and says nothing. I told the moth. It twitched one wing.
options.later: I have been calling it Wick all day. It comes when called, or when the lamp is lit. I cannot yet tell which.

options.label: Sorrel
options.reply: Sorrel. A good green name, for a grey little visitor. I said it aloud and the moth turned round once.
options.later: Sorrel has taken the left side of the lamp shade. I have taken the right. We are neighbours now, formally.

nights.text: Somewhere down the lane someone is roasting a duck. I have been standing at the door, being polite about it with my nose.
extras: A thin new moon showed up over the hedge, no wider than a fingernail clipping. I gave it a small wave.
The step was damp this morning and the boots took it personally. They are drying by the stove, sulking.
I found a button in the flour bin. Nobody will own up, so it lives on the shelf now.
A wind came round the corner and tried every window in turn. The lamp has opinions about it.

note.text: The longest evenings are for the smallest comforts.

nights.text: The moth keeps tapping the lamp shade, and I cannot hear myself think. Might we have six minutes of quiet, to let it settle?
extras: There is a fine mist on the lane this morning. The hedge looks like it is being thought about.
I have found out that a scarf can be a tablecloth, if the dinner is small enough.
The jam jar on the shelf has a new lid. I do not remember buying it, so I am calling it a gift.
Somebody has hung a lantern at the end of the lane. It makes the dark feel a little less empty.
The stove ticks as it cools, like a clock that has given up on the hour and kept the company.

quest.done: Six minutes, and the moth has folded its wings on the shade. It looks like a small grey button. Thank you.

keepsake.name: A moth-wing button
keepsake.description: A dusty grey button, light as breath, that someone left beside the lamp.

nights.text: An envelope under the door this morning, sealed with a dab of jam. Shall I open it now, or leave it by the lamp until evening?
extras: The lane is quiet today. Even the puddles are keeping still, out of courtesy.
I found a good use for the small pan: it catches the drip from the third stair. It sings a bit.
A crow sat on the fence and looked at my chimney like a landlord. I put the kettle on to seem prosperous.
The bread has gone a little hard. I am calling it hardy and eating it with soup.

note.text: Even a short day can hold a whole supper.

options.label: Open it now
options.reply: Now, then. I slid a butter knife under the flap and held my breath. The jam was raspberry. That is all I will say yet.
options.later: I read the letter twice by the window. It is short and kindly, and it smells faintly of jam. I have put it on the shelf.

options.label: Wait for evening
options.reply: Evening it is. I have propped it against the lamp, and I will try not to look at it more than twice an hour.
options.later: I opened it by lamplight, as planned. It was worth the waiting, I think. The jam had set properly by then.

nights.text: The moth was gone from the lamp shade this morning. It left a faint grey smudge shaped like a comma. I am treating it as a pause.
extras: The crescent moon is a little fatter tonight. It looks like it has been eating well.
Friday has a loose, slippered feeling. I have not done much about it.
I rubbed a clear patch in the frosty window and looked at the lane through it. The lane looked back, politely.
The wooden spoon has a new dent. I have given it a small medal.
Somewhere a gate is swinging on one hinge. It sounds like a very slow conversation.
